items.titleRaw: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.contentRaw: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ and AUC to $0.852$. Its length-corrected variant no longer shows a significant bias towards stationary trajectories and short inter-message distances, but still favors candidates farther from the RF detection. A time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting remains ahead (precision $0.9013$, AUC $0.904$), so this single-detection, hand-designed PHMM formulation approaches but does not beat it.

payloadJson.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion

items.titleRaw: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.contentRaw: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

payloadJson.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices

items.titleRaw: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.contentRaw: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

payloadJson.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots

items.titleRaw: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
items.contentRaw: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.

payloadJson.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations

items.titleRaw: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.contentRaw: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

payloadJson.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers

items.titleRaw: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.contentRaw: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.

payloadJson.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

items.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.325 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Fixed a security issue in how zstd-compressed responses are decoded
- Added a spinner tip in VS Code and similar integrated terminals about re-running a notebook cell, shown once Claude has read or edited a Jupyter notebook
- Added a line under the error shown when your organization's policy blocks a request, saying how to continue: run `/rewind` and change the message, or run `/clear`
- Added a note for Claude when a sandboxed `git checkout`, `git stash` or autostash pull cannot update protected files such as those in `.claude`
- Fixed `/security-review` and skills' inline git commands stopping with an error in worktrees of bare repositories, `--separate-git-dir` checkouts and Android `repo` checkouts
- Fixed subagents with their own model being moved to the plan-mode model when the model setting is `opusplan` or `haiku`
- Fixed subagents on a different model sizing file reads and MCP results with the main session's model
- Fixed sessions on many third-party gateways and Foundry stopping with a context length error on every turn instead of compacting
- Fixed recent turns sometimes going missing from a resumed session after Claude Code stopped without a clean exit
- Fixed shell commands running in the launch directory after the working directory was deleted; the command now fails with a message and can be re-issued
- Fixed an approved plan edit being lost when the `plansDirectory` folder can't take it: the plan is now saved in the default plans folder, and a warning says where and why
- Fixed a saved `sonnet[1m]` model setting being rewritten on a new install to a model id the API rejects
- Fixed focus view hiding the reply to your prompt when a scheduled task replied after it
- Fixed the prompt sometimes missing from a background subagent's view when fullscreen is off
- Fixed long options in lists and permission prompts being partly overwritten when they wrap, and first-run screens losing lines on narrow terminals
- Fixed startup warnings about permission rules and the "N MCP servers need authentication" notice being recorded as seen when they were scrolled out of view
- Fixed the welcome header showing control characters or splitting across lines when an agent's name or the working folder contains them or a line break

- Fixed `/stats` showing an Active days total that was one day too high
- Fixed `/insights` saying a report was ready when no session qualified for analysis, and writing two values into its HTML report without escaping them

items.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.323 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
- Added `engines["claude-code"]` to `plugin.json`: plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
- Added type checking of a plugin's TypeScript hooks module to `claude plugin validate`; each finding is a warning, and `--strict` fails on it
- Added to `claude plugin validate` the `$` nouns a mod's `engine.create` hook adds, withholds or replaces
- Added support for `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` in managed settings for Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
- Added an options menu (stop, switch to usage credits, upgrade) when a model needs usage credits that are turned off or used up
- Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in `claude -p` and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
- Added `.docx` support to Artifact tool asset uploads
- Added a `/diff to close` hint to the diff panel, and the keys that focus and close a panel to the `?` shortcut guide
- Added a start-up warning for Bash allow rules with a `*` in a variable's value, such as `Bash(PORT=* npm run dev)`
- Added a warning when a plugin's language server can't start, naming the server and what to check
- Added a one-time startup notice naming `CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE` when Perforce settings are found and the mode is off
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES` (available since 2.1.318): set it to `1` to turn off subagent progress summaries and the requests that write them (anthropics/claude-code#86879)
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_HINT_COMMAND`, which a program that starts Claude Code can set to have the exit hint name its own resume command
- Added `unsetOptionCount` to the `claude plugin install --json` result: how many `userConfig` options are not yet set
- Added `isPromptCovered` to the props a mod's pane is drawn with, telling it when a dialog or a field above the prompt covers the prompt
- Fixed running `/compact` again, or after a command such as `/context`, summarizing away a message that Claude had not answered yet
- Fixed a resumed session joining your next message to an old interrupted message that was not resumed
- Fixed a memory spike at the next prompt after Claude changed a very large file
- Fixed a setting saved in a running session undoing a hand edit made to `settings.json` moments earlier; a settings file you delete during a session now stays deleted
- Fixed `claude plugin` commands and `claude mcp list` signing you out of a Console profile when they ended while the token was being renewed
- Fixed Edit and Bash running out of memory on certain `/proc` files, and Edit hanging or running out of memory on devices and named pipes
- Fixed Claude Code failing to start, or to clear stored credentials at sign-out, when saving its configuration file failed with "Out of memory"
- Fixed requests sent without streaming failing on errors that streamed requests recover from, such as a rejected image, thinking block or beta header
- Fixed `ExitWorktree`, the worktree exit dialog and `/resume` leaving the session in the wrong folder when the folder the shell was in before entering the worktree had been deleted
- Fixed accents and other combining marks sometimes landing left of the text, leaving stale copies on screen, or silently disappearing when text wraps
- Fixed the last key of a key chord, such as Enter in ctrl+x enter, acting on a dialog's text field when the chord's own action isn't available there
- Fixed `ps` processes piling up when the process listing Claude Code runs before stopping a command takes too long
- Fixed subagent transcripts and large tool results being saved apart from the session's transcript after entering a worktree created by a `WorktreeCreate` hook or belonging to a nested repository
- Fixed a session on a named Anthropic profile moving to another sign-in when `/fork`, the Left arrow or `--bg` continued it in the background; reopen any session that was open during the update
- Fixed a background session sending a conversation under another sign-in when its named Anthropic profile is missing, changed or overridden; it now stops and says so
- Fixed a session on an API key, auth token or workload identity from its shell (not a setup token) moving to another sign-in in the background; it now stops and says so
- Fixed MCP tool calls ending in the sign-in server's error, such as `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, instead of asking you to sign in again
- Fixed an expired claude.ai login showing "Credit balance too low" when a saved Console key or `ant auth login` profile without credit was used instead
- Fixed a session on a named Anthropic profile being handed to an older background service that could not keep its sign-in; it now says to restart the service
- Fixed a background session's sign-in leaving the previous account's login or other credentials in place; it now clears them for every session on the computer, and a refused sign-in can leave no login

- Fixed sessions opened before a sign-in keeping signed-out feature flags after the sign-in
- Fixed sessions that kept failing after a Claude apps gateway sign-in expired: once you sign in again with `/login` in another terminal, they carry on at the next message
- Fixed the billing notice naming your `ant auth login` organization when a custom `X-Api-Key` header is set
- macOS: Fixed "Not logged in · Please run /login" coming back right after a successful `/login` or a token refresh when the keychain was slow to answer
- Fixed turns failing in Claude Desktop when an organization's gateway answers an expired token with 403: Claude Code now asks Desktop for a fresh token and retries
- Fixed the error shown when Amazon Bedrock refuses your account a model: it no longer says to refresh your AWS credentials, it says to enable the model
- Fixed the `awsAuthRefresh` or `gcpAuthRefresh` command sometimes running twice for one request when three or more sessions needed a fresh sign-in at once
- Fixed the `claude -p` warning about an ended claude.ai login to say that `claude auth logout` also removes saved MCP server logins and plugin secrets

- Fixed a case where some `lsof` commands ran without a permission prompt
- Fixed Bash commands that write a file with `cat > file <<EOF` being shown as "Read 1 file"

- Fixed plan files sometimes being written outside the project when `plansDirectory` is set; a write that can't be shown to stay inside the project is now refused
- Fixed a permission prompt when Claude read the output of its own background command or agent after entering a worktree
- Fixed a case where Bash permission checks missed part of a command
- Fixed a case where the Bash sandbox could switch off during a session
- Fixed Bash allow rules with an attached wildcard, such as `Bash(ls*)`, skipping the permission prompt in some cases; a rule that names a variable, such as `Bash(NODE_ENV*)`, now asks
- Fixed auto mode running behind a gateway at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on a model whose gateway name contains "haiku"; such a model, other than `claude-haiku-5-5`, is now refused, as Haiku 4.5 is
- Fixed Bash deny and ask rules missing some commands run through `sudo`, `env` and similar wrappers
- Fixed Bash allow rules written with combined `sudo` flags skipping the permission prompt in some cases
- Fixed `sandbox.excludedCommands` letting a command that it does not name run outside the sandbox in some cases
- Fixed a case where the Write and Edit tools could write to a path covered by a `Read` deny rule
- Fixed a case where a Bash command ran without a permission prompt for zsh users with certain non-default shell options set
- Fixed the Bash sandbox not fully protecting Claude Code's own config on installs still using the legacy config file
- Fixed a permission prompt from a mod's `tool.check` hook naming every plugin hooked on the tool instead of the one that asked
- Fixed sandboxed commands being able to read Claude Code's file checkpoint copies under the config directory
- Fixed a rewind sometimes changing your permission mode
- Fixed project settings sometimes being read through a symbolic link that leads to a different folder than the one Claude Code checked
- Fixed HTTP hooks failing with HTTP 500 on Linux when `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` is set and `sandbox.enabled` is off
- Fixed `claude -p` and the Agent SDK running Bash unsandboxed when `--settings` or SDK settings that turn the sandbox on fail validation; Claude Code now stops at start-up and names the invalid setting
- Fixed `/export` silently stopping early after a long run of calls to an MCP tool that is no longer loaded
- Fixed earlier MCP tool calls missing from a resumed conversation, and lines repeating in scrollback, when the server connects late
- Fixed `claude mcp add --help` splitting long example commands across lines in narrow terminals and pipes, so a pasted example ran without its header

- Fixed a timed-out feedback send being reported as too large; it now says the request timed out

release.body:
## What's changed

- Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
- Added `engines["claude-code"]` to `plugin.json`: plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
- Added type checking of a plugin's TypeScript hooks module to `claude plugin validate`; each finding is a warning, and `--strict` fails on it
- Added to `claude plugin validate` the `$` nouns a mod's `engine.create` hook adds, withholds or replaces
- Added support for `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` in managed settings for Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
- Added an options menu (stop, switch to usage credits, upgrade) when a model needs usage credits that are turned off or used up
- Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in `claude -p` and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
- Added `.docx` support to Artifact tool asset uploads
- Added a `/diff to close` hint to the diff panel, and the keys that focus and close a panel to the `?` shortcut guide
- Added a start-up warning for Bash allow rules with a `*` in a variable's value, such as `Bash(PORT=* npm run dev)`

- Fixed a hang or out-of-memory crash when a connector in a cloud session lists resources with very long names
- Fixed Remote Control showing as connected after its connection closed for good while the session's history was still uploading
- Fixed screen reader mode turning off when you return to a conversation from agent view
- Fixed screen reader mode y/n questions taking as yes a stray "y" at the end of text typed as the question opened
- Fixed cloud sessions telling Claude that a host is probably not allowed when it is allowed and the network proxy could not connect to it
- Fixed an MCP server sometimes showing as connected with no tools after it was reconnected or the session's directory changed while its tools were still loading
- Fixed Bash commands sometimes running in the wrong folder when Claude sent several at once and an earlier one changed folders
- Fixed files Claude sends from cloud and Remote Control sessions failing at once when an upload gets an HTTP 507 from a proxy; the upload now gets a second try

- Fixed sign-in, token refresh and logout waiting indefinitely when something on the network accepts the connection but never answers the TLS handshake
- Fixed a sent file showing under a different name in the Claude apps when its name hid text-direction or control characters; Claude now refuses to send such a file
- Fixed sub-agent progress summaries running a request to its end after the model replied with a tool call
- Fixed Bash reads such as `grep -r foo "$PWD/src"` asking for permission when the same command with the path typed out runs without asking
- Fixed Claude apps gateway refusing to start when a `desktop` setting holds a field newer than the gateway, such as a managed MCP server's `oauth.omitResource`; it now warns and serves it
- Fixed Bash commands coming back empty for zsh users whose `.zshrc` sets `KSH_OPTION_PRINT`
- macOS: Fixed "Unable to read managed policy settings" at startup when a valid MDM profile was slow to read: the read is retried once, and a timeout is now reported as a timeout
- Fixed agent view erasing another agent view's saved input text when it restarted for an update with nothing typed
- Fixed remote sessions giving no reply after a restart when a `UserPromptSubmit` hook blocked a replayed permission answer; these hooks no longer run on that replay

- Fixed Claude Desktop not showing spend limit warnings behind a Claude apps gateway whose policy has no `code:` rules

- Fixed the Artifact tool telling Claude to add filters when an artifact's database collection is too large to sort; it now says to read the collection page by page and sort the results
- Fixed a restarted cloud session dropping a message with a large image when the restart came before Claude's first reply to it
- Fixed a restarted cloud session leaving a subagent's message to the main conversation unanswered
- Fixed Claude not being told when you stop or pause a running workflow, so it no longer says the workflow is still running
- Improved the `/model` picker: "More models" is now an unnumbered row below every other, and older models open under it without renumbering the rest
- Gateway: Improved spend limits on a busy replica, which now skips fewer checks and records spend sooner
- Improved the Claude apps gateway's sign-in limit messages in Claude Code and on the `/device` page: they no longer name gateway settings, which the gateway's own log still names
- Improved `claude install` and the install scripts: they finish 2 to 4 seconds sooner
- Improved how soon a Remote Control session whose process crashed can pick up a new message
- Windows: Improved startup and first-command time by finding programs on PATH without starting a helper process
- Improved auto mode in headless sessions, the desktop app and VS Code: reports from background subagents that wait together are answered in one model call, as in the terminal
- Improved the agent view's row for a `claude --bg --worktree` session that couldn't set up its worktree: it now shows the error from its beginning, not an internal tag or its last 200 characters
- Improved the messages shown when an artifact is in another organization: `/login` is offered only if it's one of yours, and Claude now says where a copy may be after an account move
- Improved sessions with more images than fit in one request: Claude is told whether it has already seen a dropped image, and repeat reads of an unchanged image are limited
- Improved `claude remote-control`'s messages for an unanswered first-run question: each now says what to do next
- Improved start-up time by loading trusted TLS certificates faster
- Improved Claude apps gateway error messages to show the gateway's address without any user name or password
- Improved the Claude apps gateway's spend limit error: the reset now shows in your local time, such as "resets 4pm (America/Los_Angeles)"
- Windows: Improved startup time with a standard Git for Windows install by no longer checking which git.exe to run on every launch
- Updated the session-feedback message and the `allowedProviders` setting description to name Ultra alongside Pro and Max, and the `forceLoginMethod` description to cover every paid Claude plan
- Updated the bundled dataviz skill to suggest a list of meters, one row per item, for several ratios that each have their own limit
- Updated the "Upgrade to Max" options to say "Upgrade to Max or Ultra"
- Changed mods Claude writes to turn on without asking in auto and bypass modes, even with managed `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` or `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, and not to load in `dontAsk` mode
- Changed mods' own tool calls (`$.tool.call`, `$.mcp.call`) to raise no permission prompt, even under your own ask rules or in `dontAsk` and `-p` runs; deny rules and organization policy still apply
- Changed saved Fable 5.1 model picks to move to `fable`: on Pro and Max plans at once, on Team and Enterprise plans once your organization allows it; use `/model claude-fable-5-1` to switch back
- Changed the fast mode labels in `/fast`, `/config` and `/model` to name your current model when it supports fast mode, and removed "(Opus only)" from the VS Code row
- Changed nested skill loading: `.claude/skills` folders inside `~/.claude/plugins` no longer load when Claude works on files there
- Self-hosted runner: Changed an on-demand runner that the server refuses because it is not needed (session ended or paused, work order superseded) to exit 0 instead of 1
- Windows: Changed how Claude Code finds programs it starts itself, such as git, to skip relative and UNC PATH entries and links onto a network share, and to pick up PATH changes from settings
- Changed OpenTelemetry hook events in non-interactive sessions to leave two built-in hooks out of `num_hooks` and `num_success` after Bash and PowerShell calls
- Changed the number of messages a Claude Desktop Code tab session can send to your other sessions before it waits for you to type again from 10 to 20
- Changed `AskUserQuestion` in `claude -p` and SDK sessions to deny a host's permission answer that sets the undocumented `afkTimeoutMs` input field
- Changed managed `extraKnownMarketplaces`: a declared name can't be added from another source, an entry from elsewhere is hidden, and plugins the declared marketplace lists are reinstalled from it
- Changed Claude in Chrome tools that an app running Claude Code provides, such as the Claude desktop app's Code tab, to follow your organization's Claude in Chrome policy
- Changed `policy_mode: layered` in the Claude apps gateway: managed MCP servers now add up over every matching policy, `match: {}` included, so a gateway already on it serves more after the upgrade
- Gateway: Changed Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry upstreams to ignore the `ANTHROPIC_*_BASE_URL` variables in the gateway's environment. Set `base_url` on the upstream to use another endpoint
- Changed headless sessions to reload mods in `.claude/skills` when their files change; set `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=0` to turn this off
- Changed the Cyber Verification Program sentence on a cyber safeguard block to use the same words as claude.ai
- Changed Cowork cloud sessions: a PostToolUse hook can no longer replace the answer to AskUserQuestion or the plan in ExitPlanMode's result; Claude reads the originals
- Changed `cp` and `mv` spelled by a path, such as `/bin/cp`, to get the same path checks as `cp` and `mv`
- Changed background command notifications and TaskStop results to show Claude only the start and end of a command over 1,000 characters, which saves context
- Changed artifact design guidance to treat Inter and Space Grotesk as good default typefaces
- Changed the account email check to refuse only a shell command that holds your email and names a User-Agent, without asking, so other commands and scheduled runs no longer stop at its prompt
- Changed Remote Control sessions to keep the folder they were started in: a connected client can no longer move a session to another folder
- Changed managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` take-overs from an undeclared source: saved data is set aside for `cleanupPeriodDays`, and options and secrets until `claude plugin restore-set-aside`
- [VSCode] Added a warning above the prompt box when both an auth token and an API key are set, matching the terminal's startup warning
- [VSCode] Fixed a plugin's permission request showing a name with hidden characters: it now reads "a plugin"

- Improved the agent view's row for a `claude --bg --worktree` session that couldn't set up its worktree: it now shows the error from its beginning, not an internal tag or its last 200 characters
- Improved the messages shown when an artifact is in another organization: `/login` is offered only if it's one of yours, and Claude now says where a copy may be after an account move
- Improved sessions with more images than fit in one request: Claude is told whether it has already seen a dropped image, and repeat reads of an unchanged image are limited
- Improved `claude remote-control`'s messages for an unanswered first-run question: each now says what to do next
- Improved start-up time by loading trusted TLS certificates faster
- Improved Claude apps gateway error messages to show the gateway's address without any user name or password
- Improved the Claude apps gateway's spend limit error: the reset now shows in your local time, such as "resets 4pm (America/Los_Angeles)"
- Windows: Improved startup time with a standard Git for Windows install by no longer checking which git.exe to run on every launch
- Updated the session-feedback message and the `allowedProviders` setting description to name Ultra alongside Pro and Max, and the `forceLoginMethod` description to cover every paid Claude plan
- Updated the bundled dataviz skill to suggest a list of meters, one row per item, for several ratios that each have their own limit
- Updated the "Upgrade to Max" options to say "Upgrade to Max or Ultra"
- Changed mods Claude writes to turn on without asking in auto and bypass modes, even with managed `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` or `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, and not to load in `dontAsk` mode
- Changed mods' own tool calls (`$.tool.call`, `$.mcp.call`) to raise no permission prompt, even under your own ask rules or in `dontAsk` and `-p` runs; deny rules and organization policy still apply
- Changed saved Fable 5.1 model picks to move to `fable`: on Pro and Max plans at once, on Team and Enterprise plans once your organization allows it; use `/model claude-fable-5-1` to switch back
- Changed the fast mode labels in `/fast`, `/config` and `/model` to name your current model when it supports fast mode, and removed "(Opus only)" from the VS Code row
- Changed nested skill loading: `.claude/skills` folders inside `~/.claude/plugins` no longer load when Claude works on files there
- Self-hosted runner: Changed an on-demand runner that the server refuses because it is not needed (session ended or paused, work order superseded) to exit 0 instead of 1
- Windows: Changed how Claude Code finds programs it starts itself, such as git, to skip relative and UNC PATH entries and links onto a network share, and to pick up PATH changes from settings
- Changed OpenTelemetry hook events in non-interactive sessions to leave two built-in hooks out of `num_hooks` and `num_success` after Bash and PowerShell calls
- Changed the number of messages a Claude Desktop Code tab session can send to your other sessions before it waits for you to type again from 10 to 20
- Changed `AskUserQuestion` in `claude -p` and SDK sessions to deny a host's permission answer that sets the undocumented `afkTimeoutMs` input field
- Changed managed `extraKnownMarketplaces`: a declared name can't be added from another source, an entry from elsewhere is hidden, and plugins the declared marketplace lists are reinstalled from it
- Changed Claude in Chrome tools that an app running Claude Code provides, such as the Claude desktop app's Code tab, to follow your organization's Claude in Chrome policy
- Changed `policy_mode: layered` in the Claude apps gateway: managed MCP servers now add up over every matching policy, `match: {}` included, so a gateway already on it serves more after the upgrade
- Gateway: Changed Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry upstreams to ignore the `ANTHROPIC_*_BASE_URL` variables in the gateway's environment. Set `base_url` on the upstream to use another endpoint
- Changed headless sessions to reload mods in `.claude/skills` when their files change; set `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=0` to turn this off
- Changed the Cyber Verification Program sentence on a cyber safeguard block to use the same words as claude.ai
- Changed Cowork cloud sessions: a PostToolUse hook can no longer replace the answer to AskUserQuestion or the plan in ExitPlanMode's result; Claude reads the originals
- Changed `cp` and `mv` spelled by a path, such as `/bin/cp`, to get the same path checks as `cp` and `mv`
- Changed background command notifications and TaskStop results to show Claude only the start and end of a command over 1,000 characters, which saves context
- Changed artifact design guidance to treat Inter and Space Grotesk as good default typefaces
- Changed the account email check to refuse only a shell command that holds your email and names a User-Agent, without asking, so other commands and scheduled runs no longer stop at its prompt
- Changed Remote Control sessions to keep the folder they were started in: a connected client can no longer move a session to another folder
- Changed managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` take-overs from an undeclared source: saved data is set aside for `cleanupPeriodDays`, and options and secrets until `claude plugin restore-set-aside`
- [VSCode] Added a warning above the prompt box when both an auth token and an API key are set, matching the terminal's startup warning
- [VSCode] Fixed a plugin's permission request showing a name with hidden characters: it now reads "a plugin"

items.titleRaw: huggingface/transformers v5.23.0 released
items.contentRaw: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/jev) * Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in [#50054](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50054) ### LFM3 LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. The attention layers apply RMSNorm to the query and key heads and gate their output with a per-head sigmoid. Every layer applies a sandwich norm to the operator and feed-forward outputs before the residual addition. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-Text (#50322) by @paulpak58 in [#50322](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50322) ### Dots 3 Note Preview Dots 3 Note Preview is a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video, and audio inputs. It uses a shared vision encoder for images and videos and a Whisper-style audio encoder, and both encoders project their outputs into the language model's hidden space before autoregressive text generation. BF16 and FP8 inference are supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/dots3_note) * Add dots3-note Preview model support (#47844) by @miraclezqc in [#47844](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/47844) ### LFM3-VL LFM3-VL is a vision-language model family from Liquid AI, built on the LFM3 language model. It takes images and videos at their native resolution together with text. It combines a hybrid vision encoder (a linear patchifier, gated depthwise 2D convolution layers, and bidirectional grouped-query attention layers with 2D rotary embeddings) with a projector and an LFM3 language model. The projector merges each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token through a layer norm and a two-layer MLP. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3_vl) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-VL (#50392) by @paulpak58 in [#50392](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50392) ### IQuestCoder IQuest-Coder-V1 is a family of code language models developed by IQuest Lab, available in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants. Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the Transformers auto classes load it with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only IQuestCoderConfig is specific to IQuestCoder. The looped `IQuest-Coder-V1-*-Loop-*` checkpoints use a different architecture and aren't supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/iquestcoder) * Add IQuestCoder (#50579) by @hmellor in [#50579](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50579) ### InternLM3 InternLM3 is an 8B instruction-tuned language model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory (checkpoint: internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct). Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load it with the Llama implementation (LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM), and only InternLM3Config is specific to InternLM3. The config names the attention biases `qkv_bias` and the output projection and MLP biases `bias`. InternLM3Config loads these as `attention_bias` and `mlp_bias` and requires them to be equal, as they are in the released checkpoints. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/internlm3) * Add InternLM3 (#50578) by @hmellor in [#50578](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50578) ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Remove the `ep_router` expert-parallel style (#49615) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Run MXFP4 GPT-OSS experts through `ep_dispatch_experts` (#49613) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 `deepgemm_megamoe` EP implementation for DeepGEMM Mega MoE (#49606) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Slim down `[audio]` to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr (drop librosa and phonemizer) (#50610) by @eustlb * 🚨 Deprecate Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM and pyctcdecode/kenlm LM decoding (#50408) by @eustlb * 🚨 Exporters: `ExportedModel`, Hub save/load, one backend registry (#50029) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Move processing defaults to class (#49089) by @guarin * :rotating_light: [`kernels`] Bump version (#50307) by @vasqu * :rotating_light: Finally drop rope deltas from ModelOutput! (#50153) by @zucchini-nlp * 🚨 Safe-ize pi0 graphs (#50160) by @molbap * 🚨 [serve][breaking] update attn for mac users (#49730) by @SunMarc * 🚨 build and expand once the tp/ep_plan/fsdp_plan (#49527) by @3outeille ## Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend (#50029, #50032, #50309, #50311) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b17b2ab-b2b8-4e34-a983-4a7177330e4e Every export now returns an `ExportedModel`. You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime. The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch. ```python from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer from transformers.exporters import ExportedModel, OnnxConfig, OnnxExporter model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") inputs = tokenizer(["Exporters are here!"], return_tensors="pt") exported = OnnxExporter().export(model, inputs, OnnxConfig(dynamic=True, ort_fusions="cuda")) exported.push_to_hub("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx") exported_model = ExportedModel.from_pretrained("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx", device="cuda") outputs = exported_model(**inputs) # same output class as model(**inputs) ``` - **Fused for the runtime**: `OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda" | "webgpu" | "dml")` rewrites the graph into ONNX Runtime's fused transformer ops at export time: attention, `GroupQueryAttention` over the KV cache, rotary, norms and `MoE`. OpenVINO exports now hit OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels for attention, RoPE, MoE experts and compressed int8/int4 weights, which makes decode 2.4–3.9× faster than before. - **Faster than `torch.compile`**: on EmbeddingGemma2 (8 × 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is 7.6× faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4× faster than `torch.compile` on an A100. OpenVINO is 4.1× faster than eager and 2.2× faster than `torch.compile` on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9× and 2.6× with int8 weights). - **Shareable**: an export saves and loads like a model, optionally in a `subfolder` of the model repo. Its `export.json` records the config, input shapes, package versions and I/O names. Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way. 🚨 `export()` returns an `ExportedModel`, and an ONNX program is an `onnx_ir.Model`. `OnnxConfig`'s and `OpenVINOConfig`'s `output_path` options are gone in favour of `save_pretrained`. Custom backends register with `register_backend`. 📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/exporters ## Vision This release fixes a range of vision-model bugs: classification pipelines now respect `problem_type`, and several models get corrected behavior (Step3.7 RoPE axis order, MiniMax-M3-VL packed attention isolation, Qwen VL positions with reused caches, PaddleOCR-VL interpolation alignment, Kosmos2 SDPA masking, and Emu3 float image handling). Chunked prefill now keeps image inputs on the * fix(pipelines): respect problem_type in image and video classification pipelines (#50582) by @surendra902 in [#50582] * Fix Step3.7 vision RoPE spatial W/H axis order (#50547) by @caohch-1 in [#50547] * Raise ValueError for out-of-range float images in convert_to_rgb (#50487) by @n24q02m in [#50487] * CI: install OpenVINO and NNCF in the daily GPU image (#50422) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#50422] * Fix MiniMax-M3-VL packed vision attention isolation (#50346) by @taking-lying-flat in [#50346] * Fix Qwen VL positions when a text cache is reused with a new image (#50427) by @Arnav66692 in [#50427] * [Docker] Update Nvidia CI and Flash Attn CI images to torch 2.15 / cu132 (#50467) by @ydshieh in [#50467] * Fix PaddleOCR-VL vision position interpolation alignment (#50384) by @scyyh11 in [#50384] * Fix Emu3 image processor crash on float numpy images (#50226) by @simpleqt in [#50226] * Build Idefics-style vision position ids with torch.where (#49917) by @shoumikhin in [#49917] * Keep image inputs on the first chunk of a chunked prefill (#49753) by @digit50 in [#49753] * Docs: note in the v5 migration guide that hidden_states[-1] of vision models is pre-norm (#50303) by @ravediamond in [#50303] * Remove the GitHub API cache-bust from the AMD docker images (#49351) by @tarekziade in [#49351] * [docs] Vision backend differences (#50131) by @stevhliu in [#50131] * [Kosmos2] Fix SDPA applying a causal mask in the image-to-text projection (#50118) by @tarekziade in [#50118] ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. Expert parallelism gains a selectable `ep_implementation` (all-reduce for CUDA-graph-friendly inference, all-to-all for training). The Trainer now reduces FSDP/HSDP gradients only on the last micro-batch, and the token-count normalization is fixed to use true division. release.body: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/jev) * Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in [#50054](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50054) ### LFM3 LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. The attention layers apply RMSNorm to the query and key heads and gate their output with a per-head sigmoid. Every layer applies a sandwich norm to the operator and feed-forward outputs before the residual addition. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-Text (#50322) by @paulpak58 in [#50322](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50322) ### Dots 3 Note Preview Dots 3 Note Preview is a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video, and audio inputs. It uses a shared vision encoder for images and videos and a Whisper-style audio encoder, and both encoders project their outputs into the language model's hidden space before autoregressive text generation. BF16 and FP8 inference are supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/dots3_note) * Add dots3-note Preview model support (#47844) by @miraclezqc in [#47844](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/47844) ### LFM3-VL LFM3-VL is a vision-language model family from Liquid AI, built on the LFM3 language model. It takes images and videos at their native resolution together with text. It combines a hybrid vision encoder (a linear patchifier, gated depthwise 2D convolution layers, and bidirectional grouped-query attention layers with 2D rotary embeddings) with a projector and an LFM3 language model. The projector merges each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token through a layer norm and a two-layer MLP. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3_vl) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-VL (#50392) by @paulpak58 in [#50392](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50392) ### IQuestCoder IQuest-Coder-V1 is a family of code language models developed by IQuest Lab, available in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants. Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the Transformers auto classes load it with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only IQuestCoderConfig is specific to IQuestCoder. The looped `IQuest-Coder-V1-*-Loop-*` checkpoints use a different architecture and aren't supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/iquestcoder) * Add IQuestCoder (#50579) by @hmellor in [#50579](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50579) ### InternLM3 InternLM3 is an 8B instruction-tuned language model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory (checkpoint: internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct). Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load it with the Llama implementation (LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM), and only InternLM3Config is specific to InternLM3. The config names the attention biases `qkv_bias` and the output projection and MLP biases `bias`. InternLM3Config loads these as `attention_bias` and `mlp_bias` and requires them to be equal, as they are in the released checkpoints. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/internlm3) * Add InternLM3 (#50578) by @hmellor in [#50578](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50578) ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Remove the `ep_router` expert-parallel style (#49615) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Run MXFP4 GPT-OSS experts through `ep_dispatch_experts` (#49613) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 `deepgemm_megamoe` EP implementation for DeepGEMM Mega MoE (#49606) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Slim down `[audio]` to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr (drop librosa and phonemizer) (#50610) by @eustlb * 🚨 Deprecate Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM and pyctcdecode/kenlm LM decoding (#50408) by @eustlb * 🚨 Exporters: `ExportedModel`, Hub save/load, one backend registry (#50029) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Move processing defaults to class (#49089) by @guarin * :rotating_light: [`kernels`] Bump version (#50307) by @vasqu * :rotating_light: Finally drop rope deltas from ModelOutput! (#50153) by @zucchini-nlp * 🚨 Safe-ize pi0 graphs (#50160) by @molbap * 🚨 [serve][breaking] update attn for mac users (#49730) by @SunMarc * 🚨 build and expand once the tp/ep_plan/fsdp_plan (#49527) by @3outeille ## Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend (#50029, #50032, #50309, #50311) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b17b2ab-b2b8-4e34-a983-4a7177330e4e Every export now returns an `ExportedModel`. You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime. The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch. ```python from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer from transformers.exporters import ExportedModel, OnnxConfig, OnnxExporter model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") inputs = tokenizer(["Exporters are here!"], return_tensors="pt") exported = OnnxExporter().export(model, inputs, OnnxConfig(dynamic=True, ort_fusions="cuda")) exported.push_to_hub("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx") exported_model = ExportedModel.from_pretrained("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx", device="cuda") outputs = exported_model(**inputs) # same output class as model(**inputs) ``` - **Fused for the runtime**: `OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda" | "webgpu" | "dml")` rewrites the graph into ONNX Runtime's fused transformer ops at export time: attention, `GroupQueryAttention` over the KV cache, rotary, norms and `MoE`. OpenVINO exports now hit OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels for attention, RoPE, MoE experts and compressed int8/int4 weights, which makes decode 2.4–3.9× faster than before. - **Faster than `torch.compile`**: on EmbeddingGemma2 (8 × 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is 7.6× faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4× faster than `torch.compile` on an A100. OpenVINO is 4.1× faster than eager and 2.2× faster than `torch.compile` on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9× and 2.6× with int8 weights). - **Shareable**: an export saves and loads like a model, optionally in a `subfolder` of the model repo. Its `export.json` records the config, input shapes, package versions and I/O names. Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way. 🚨 `export()` returns an `ExportedModel`, and an ONNX program is an `onnx_ir.Model`. `OnnxConfig`'s and `OpenVINOConfig`'s `output_path` options are gone in favour of `save_pretrained`. Custom backends register with `register_backend`. 📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/exporters ## Vision This release fixes a range of vision-model bugs: classification pipelines now respect `problem_type`, and several models get corrected behavior (Step3.7 RoPE axis order, MiniMax-M3-VL packed attention isolation, Qwen VL positions with reused caches, PaddleOCR-VL interpolation alignment, Kosmos2 SDPA masking, and Emu3 float image handling). items.contentRaw: ## New Models ### Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe. Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union. #### Key Features Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices: - **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert. - **1M context length**, for long-context workloads. - **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. - **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request. Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities: - **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run. - **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights. - **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union. - **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts. - **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement. - **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests. - **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window. The model is released under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. #### Recommended Settings - **Reasoning Effort**: - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`. - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage. - **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: - `temperature=1.0` - `top_p=0.95` - **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. - **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. - **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille ## Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and `is_trainable` is now `True`. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. items.contentRaw:
## MiMo V2.6

Xiaomi MiMo's [mimo-v2.6](https://ollama.com/library/mimo-v2.6), a 9B model built for code and agent workflows, is now supported in Ollama.

```sh
ollama run mimo-v2.6
```

## AutoTrust decision models

[AutoTrust](https://ollama.com/library/autotrust-jev) decision models read text and return choices, yes or no probabilities, and ratings for the questions you supply. The family includes 9b, 35b, and 27b-vl sizes — the 35b and 27b-vl sizes can also read images.

```sh
ollama run autotrust-jev "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: autotrust-jev is supported on Apple silicon in this release.

## What's Changed

 - ollama launch now supports Kimi Code CLI — the successor to kimi-cli — and offers to migrate existing kimi-cli setups
 - ollama launch now fills in Pi's model list automatically so models can be picked inside Pi, and Claude Desktop's model
   picker shows Ollama's actual model names
 - Recurrent and vision GGUF models can now serve more than one request at a time
 - Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models using long-context (YaRN) scaling
 - Running ollama with no arguments opens the welcome launcher

* `ollama launch claude` now applies the model's output token limit for Claude Code, so cloud models no longer run into the 128k default cap
* Cloud web search responses on `/api/chat` are now decoded correctly, including compressed responses
* OpenAI-compatible endpoints no longer override a model's packaged sampler defaults — clients that send no `temperature`/`top_p` get the model's own values instead of 1.0, matching `/api/chat`
* `/v1/responses` now preserves readable input content, including prior assistant refusals, instead of flattening it
* Ollama's app can now retry ChatGPT disconnect failures instead of leaving the connection in a broken state
* `ollama launch codex` verifies ChatGPT routing before configuring, and reports a clear error when routing is unavailable
* Faster top-k sampling on MLX for large vocabularies

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

items.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
items.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
